question: Should affected timer values above Node's native ceiling become immediate hard manifest errors, or should Crabline preserve configuration compatibility through normalization or a longer-duration scheduling strategy?
rationale: The current patch correctly prevents Node's unsafe overflow behavior but intentionally turns previously accepted configuration into a validation failure, and tests alone cannot establish the desired upgrade contract.

options.title: Hard reject with recovery guidance
options.body: Retain the ceiling, prove the upgrade-time diagnostic, and provide a clear supported replacement value or recovery instruction in PR/release context.

options.title: Normalize to the ceiling
options.body: Clamp over-ceiling values with an explicit warning, preserving startup compatibility while changing the configured duration.

options.title: Support longer logical timers
options.body: Implement chunked or deadline-based scheduling so durations above the native setTimeout ceiling remain representable without schema rejection.

recommendation.title: Hard reject with recovery guidance
recommendation.body: Retain the ceiling, prove the upgrade-time diagnostic, and provide a clear supported replacement value or recovery instruction in PR/release context.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects this person most directly to the proposed timer guardrail and adjacent configuration/runtime safety work.
